definitions.explanation: Selfish attitude or behavior that prioritizes one's own desires over others. From English 'ego.' Carries a strongly negative connotation in Japanese, closer to 'selfishness' than the neutral psychological sense.

examples.japanese: ⟦{親|おや}→親：01357_oya⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧エゴ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{子|こ}ども⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{押|お}し{付|つ}ける→押し付ける：04236_oshitsukeru⟧な。
examples.english: Don't force your parental ego on your children.

examples.japanese: ⟦{環境|かんきょう}{保護|ほご}→環境保護：15308_kankyouhogo⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{訴|うった}え→訴える：01891_uttaeru⟧⟦ながら→ながら：10530_nagara⟧⟦{車|くるま}→車：00516_kuruma⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{乗|の}る→乗る：00511_noru⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、エゴ⟦ではないか→ではないか：30627_dehanaika⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われた→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: I was told that driving a car while advocating for environmental protection is hypocritical selfishness.

notes:
Borrowed from English 'ego,' but in Japanese this word almost always carries a negative connotation of selfishness — it is rarely used in the neutral psychological or philosophical sense. When Japanese speakers say エゴ, they typically mean someone is acting selfishly or imposing their own desires.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- エゴ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{通|とお}す→通す：02300_toosu⟧: to push through one's selfish desires
- エゴ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{押|お}し{付|つ}ける→押し付ける：04236_oshitsukeru⟧: to force one's selfishness on others
- ⟦{親|おや}→親：01357_oya⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧エゴ: parental selfishness
- エゴイスト: egoist; selfish person
- エゴイズム: egoism

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {我|わ}がまま: selfishness; willfulness — more colloquial and broader in usage, common in everyday speech
- {自己中|じこちゅう}: self-centered (abbreviation of ⟦{自己中心的|じこちゅうしんてき}→自己中心的：18144_jikochuushinteki⟧) — casual/slang, very common among younger speakers
- ⟦{利己的|りこてき}→利己的：21285_rikoteki⟧: selfish; self-interested — more formal and literary
